Sub-Award Description:
THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS TO STUDY HOW THE BASELINE STATE AND FUNCTION OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES CAN BE ALTERED BY VACCINATION AND DISEASE STATE, IN THE CONTEXT OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE INNATE CELL REPROGRAMMING BY VACCINATION AND BACTERIAL EXPOSURE AS WELL AS THE IMPACT ON THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE AND BACTERIAL CONTROL. THE SUBAWARD WILL PERFORM EPIGENETIC ANALYSIS OF HUMAN AND MOUSE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER LABORATORIES IN THE CONSORTIUM TO LINK MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC STATES TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES.

1)	PERFORM ATAC-SEQ EPIGENETIC PROFILING AND ANALYSIS ON ADDITIONAL FROZEN HUMAN ADHERENT BAL SAMPLES FROM
ACTIVE TB, RESISTER, HEALTHY CONTROLS, AND ASYMPTOMATIC TB INDIVIDUALS. PROFILING INCLUDES: CELL PREPARATION, TRANSPOSITION REACTION AND PURIFICATION, PCR AMPLIFICATION, LIBRARY PURIFICATION, AND LIBRARY QC. ANALYSIS
INCLUDES: SEQUENCING FILTERING AND ALIGNMENT, DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, PATHWAY ANALYSIS, AND MOTIF ENRICHMENT ANALYSIS.

2)	ANALYZE LINKAGE BETWEEN HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC PROFILES AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES (IN COLLABORATION WITH WALZL/DU PLESSIS LABS).

3)	COMPARE HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC PROFILES TO EPIGENETIC PROFILES OF MURINE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES TRAINED BY TYPE I OR TYPE II INTERFERONS.

4)	TRANSCRIPTIONAL ANALYSIS OF SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQUENCING DATA FROM HUMAN MACROPHAGES PROFILED FROM NONADHERENT BAL SAMPLES (IN COLLABORATION WITH WALZL/DU PLESSIS/LEWINSOHN LABS).

5)	COMPLETE STUDIES COMPARING INNATE RESPONSES AND PRODUCTION OF IFN-BETA FOR WT, SP140-/-, IFNAR-/-, AND SP140-/-IFNAR-/- MEXAMS AND BMDMS FOLLOWING STIMULATION WITH LPS OR INFECTION WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS TO CHARACTERIZE MACROPHAGE SUBSET-SPECIFIC REGULATION OF TYPE I IFN AND CYTOKINE RESPONSES.

Sub-Awardee Name: BETH ISRAEL DEACONESS MEDICAL CENTER, INC.
Sub-Award Description:
STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – BAROUCH LAB

DURING THE PRECEDING YEARS OF THE AWARD, WE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AN INNOVATIVE AND PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT MOUSE CHALLENGE MODEL THAT UNDERGOES REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE MTB EXPOSURES TO ASSESS THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF TB VACCINES. IN YEAR 6, WE SUCCESSFULLY ESTABLISHED AND VALIDATED A HIGHLY REPRODUCIBLE MURINE REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE CHALLENGE MODEL WITH REDUCED STRINGENCY. USING THIS MODEL, WE TESTED THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF BCGS AND ΔLPRG VACCINES. UNDER THE REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE EXPOSURE MODEL, ΔLPRG IMMUNIZATION CONFERRED ~65% PROTECTION AGAINST ACQUISITION OF INFECTION, COMPARED WITH ~45% PROTECTION OBSERVED WITH THE SINGLE ULTRA-LOW DOSE CHALLENGE, REPRESENTING A SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT IN VACCINE-INDUCED PROTECTION. WE ALSO EXPANDED OUR CORRELATES OF PROTECTION ANALYSES TO IDENTIFY CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH PROTECTION FROM THE ACQUISITION OF INFECTION. A MANUSCRIPT DESCRIBING THESE FINDINGS IS CURRENTLY IN PREPARATION.

IN YEAR 7, BASED ON THE DATA COLLECTED DURING THE PRECEDING YEAR, OUR RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON EXTENDING CORRELATES OF PROTECTION STUDIES AND CONDUCTING MECHANISTIC ANALYSES TO DEFINE THE CELLULAR SUBSETS AND PATHWAYS UNDERLYING VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION. WE WILL FURTHER CHARACTERIZE INFECTION KINETICS AND IMMUNE RESPONSES TO REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE MTB EXPOSURE MODEL TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW LOW-LEVEL MTB EXPOSURE SHAPES HOST IMMUNITY AND SUBSEQUENT INFECTION OUTCOMES. TO PERFORM THESE STUDIES, WE WILL UTILIZE A BARCODED MTB STRAIN TO MONITOR INFECTION DYNAMICS UNDER REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE AEROSOL CHALLENGES. FINALLY, WE WILL ALSO APPLY THIS PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT CHALLENGE MODEL TO EVALUATE THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF EMERGING TB VACCINES, INCLUDING SUBUNIT MRNA, PROTEIN-BASED, AND LIVE-ATTENUATED VACCINES.
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

Sub-Award Description:
STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – HAWN

THE HAWN LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL HAVE SEVERAL ROLES IN THIS SUBCONTRACT IN YEAR 7. EACH ACTIVITY FROM YEARS 1-6 IS ONGOING.

1)	 UW WILL OVERSEE GENOTYPING AND ANALYSIS OF CANDIDATE GENE POLYMORPHISMS IN HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. GENOTYPING IS COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR NEW ENROLLEES. ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH NEW CANDIDATE GENES THAT HAVE RECENTLY BEEN SELECTED FOR WORK IN YEAR 6. POLYMORPHISMS WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MTB-INFECTED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES. CANDIDATE GENES WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON STUDIES FROM DRS. URDAHL, PICKER, LEWINSOHN, AND WALZL.
2)	UW WILL ORGANIZE AND FACILITATE THE ISOLATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES AND MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES FOR EX VIVO MTB INFECTION FROM HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. MONOCYTES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS, WHICH ARE AVAILABLE FROM AN ESTABLISHED SEATTLE COHORT OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. ANALYSES ARE UNDERWAY TO EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF GENETIC VARIANTS IN CANDIDATE GENES WITH MTB-INDUCED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES IN A COHORT OF 100 HEALTHY DONORS. 
3)	CELLULAR GWAS:  UW WILL PERFORM CELLULAR GWAS EXPERIMENTS TO DISCOVER GENETIC REGULATORS OF MTB-INDUCED MYELOID CELL PHENOTYPES.  LEAD FINDINGS WILL BE ASSESSED FOR ASSOCIATION WITH CLINICAL PHENOTYPES WITH AN OVERALL GOAL TO DISCOVER MAJOR GENETIC DETERMINANTS OF TB CLINICAL PHENOTYPES.
4)	UW WILL OVERSEE THE MACROPHAGE EXPERIMENTS INCLUDING CRISPR/CAS9 GENE SILENCING IN THP1 AND U937 CELLS AND STUDIES OF PRIMARY MONOCYTES FROM SEATTLE AND CAPE TOWN. STUDIES WILL INCLUDE INFECTION OF MACROPHAGES WITH MTB AND ANALYSIS OF IMMUNE PATHWAYS AND CONTROL OF MTB REPLICATION. CELL SUPERNATANTS WILL BE HARVESTED FOR CYTOKINE/CHEMOKINE ELISA AND RNA EXTRACTED FROM CELLS, QUANTIFIED, AND ANALYZED.
5)	UW WILL COLLABORATE WITH INVESTIGATORS ON THE ANALYSIS OF WHETHER POLYMORPHISMS IN CANDIDATE GENES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES AND PREPARE IT FOR PUBLICATION WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS.

THE DU PLESSIS/WALZL LABORATORY AT STELLENBOSCH UNIVERSITY (SU) WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CLINICAL AND IMMUNOLOGICAL WORK (INCLUDING ON-SITE DATA MANAGEMENT) OF THE PROJECT. SU WILL COORDINATE THE STUDY DESIGN, PARTICIPANT SCREENING AND ENROLLMENT FOR THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, PERFORM BRONCHOSCOPIES AND MANAGE SAMPLE SHARING TO PARTICIPATING SITES. SU WILL PROVIDE INPUT IN THE DESIGN, EXECUTION AND DATA ANALYSIS OF IMMUNOLOGICAL STUDIES AND PARTICIPATE IN THE LEADERSHIP TEAM OF “CASCADE IMPAC-TB” CENTER. SU WILL INTERACT AND COORDINATE ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WITH THE PI OF THE PROJECT. DR. DU PLESSIS AND DR. WALZL, THE SU CO-PI’S WILL REVIEW ALL RAW DATA GENERATED BY THE SU TEAM, AND SUPERVISE THE LABORATORY WORK, AND THE RESEARCH TECHNICIANS. SPECIFIC DELIVERABLES FOR YEAR 7 OF THE CONTRACT AT SU INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING:

A.	RECRUITMENT: 
SU WILL CONDUCT PET/CT, BRONCHOSCOPY AND PHLEBOTOMY IN ALL COHORTS TO COVER THE FULL SPECTRUM OF INFECTION AND OBTAIN BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES FROM EACH. RECRUITMENT HAS BEEN COMPLETED, AND NO NEW PARTICIPANTS ARE BEING ENROLLED. HOWEVER, WE ARE FOLLOWING UP SELECTED PARTICIPANTS TO SCREEN FOR TB PROGRESSION WITH LONGITUDINAL SAMPLING, REQUIRING ETHICS APPROVAL AND LIMITED CONTINUED CLINICAL INVOLVEMENT.

B. END-ASSAYS: 

IMMUNOPHENOTYPING EXPERIMENTS – ONE OF THE DELIVERABLES AT SU IS TO CONDUCT DEEP PHENOTYPING OF PAIRED BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL) AND PBMC FROM THE VARIOUS CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY CLINICAL GROUPS. SU HAS EVALUATED THE ASSAY PRIORITY LIST, AS WELL AS THE BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED IN THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, TO ENUMERATE THE NUMBER OF STORED SAMPLES AVAILABLE FOR THE OBJECTIVES RELATED TO THE PROPOSED PLANS FOR THIS END-ASSAY. OF ALL MAIN STUDY PARTICIPANTS FROM WHICH PAIRED BAL AND PBMC HAVE BEEN COLLECTED, SUFFICIENT CELL NUMBERS WERE OBTAINED FROM 88% OF PARTICIPANTS, WHICH INCLUDES MAKING USE OF RESIDUALLY STORED BAL CELLS. WE WILL PERFORM MULTIPARAMETER FLOW CYTOMETRY ANALYSES ON UNFRACTIONATED BAL CELLS AND PBMC SAMPLES FROM A SUBSET OF INDIVIDUALS FROM THE CASCADE CLINICAL GROUPS ALL COHORTS TO DEFINE THE PHENOTYPE OF LUNG RESIDENT AND CIRCULATING LYMPHOCYTE POPULATIONS.  IMMUNE PHENOTYPING OF THESE SU HHC PBMC SAMPLES FOR THE LYMPHOID FLOW CYTOMETRY PANEL WILL BE COMPLETED BY MARCH 2026. 

GRANULOMA MODEL/KILLING ASSAYS – SU WILL MAKE USE OF THE IN VITRO GRANULOMA MODEL ALONG WITH PARALLEL ASSESSMENTS IN MONOLAYER CULTURE AND UNFRACTIONATED PBMC AND BAL, TO ASSESS MTB KILLING AMONGST THE VARIOUS CLINICAL GROUPS. INTERESTING FINDINGS RELATED TO MTB CONTROL WILL BE TESTED IN FUTURE IN GRANULOMA MODEL EXPERIMENTS. BY USING CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM PARTICIPANTS NOT ELIGIBLE ACCORDING TO THE CASCADE HHC STUDY CRITERIA, SU HAS OPTIMIZED THE MODEL AND ALSO IMPLEMENTED CHANGES TO STREAMLINE BACTERIAL LOAD ASSESSMENT THROUGH MGIT CULTURE. SU HAS COMPLETED THE KILLING ASSAY EXPERIMENTS FOR A QUARTER OF ALL SU HHC SAMPLES FROM 4 CLINICAL GROUPS BY THE END OF PERIOD 6 AND WILL REVIEW FINDINGS FROM THIS SUBSET OF THE COHORT PRIOR TO CONTINUING THE KILLING ASSAYS IN THE FINAL YEAR (PERIOD 7 ONWARDS).

C. OTHER LABORATORY WORK: THE RNASEQ DATA FROM THE BAL AM AND PAX SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM THE SU CASCADE HHC STUDY, ARE BEING GENERATED IN THREE RANDOMIZED BATCHES. DATA FROM ALL 3 BATCHES HAVE BEEN RECEIVED AND ARE BEING ANALYZED BY LOCAL BIOINFORMATICIANS, IT HAS BECOME EVIDENT THAT THE COMPLEXITY OF THE DATA REQUIRES MORE ADVANCED COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSES TO ACHIEVE RELIABLE AND FAST RESULTS. STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – GALE

THE GALE LABORATORY WILL PERFORM RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES IN YEAR 7. WHOLE BLOOD AND TISSUE SAMPLES WILL BE RECEIVED AT THE GALE LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA FROM LOUIS PICKER (OHSU). RNA-SEQ ASSAYS WILL BE CONDUCTED BY UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA GENOME CENTER (UMGC). RNA-SEQ ASSAY TASKS INCLUDE 1) RNA ISOLATION AND RNA QC, 2) RNA-SEQ LIBRARY CONSTRUCTION AND LIBRARY QC, AND 3) GENERATION OF RNA SEQUENCE DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES ON A UG 100 PLATFORM.

THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT COMPUTATIONAL DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELING ON THE RNA-SEQ DATA SETS. IN YEAR 7, THE GALE LAB WILL ANALYZE NHP WHOLE BLOOD AND TISSUE RNA-SEQ DATA SETS THAT WERE GENERATED IN YEAR 7 AND PRIOR PERIODS. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO INITIAL DATA QC, GENERATION OF NORMALIZED EXPRESSION MATRICES, DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, CO-EXPRESSION ANALYSIS AND WHEN APPROPRIATE RULE-BASED MODELING.

Sub-Award Description:
STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – GERNER	 

THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB), THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN.

IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MTB SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE DIVERSIFICATION OF MTB STATES AND EXPRESSION OF DIFFERENT ANTIGENS IN DIFFERENT TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS AND CELL TYPES, AND STUDY HOW THIS CORRESPONDS TO LOCAL IMMUNE ACTIVITY BY MTB-SPECIFIC T CELLS. IN YEAR 7, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL:

I. CONTINUE IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MTB INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. SUBSTANTIAL EFFORT WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING STUDIES DESCRIBING MTB DISSEMINATION TO LUNG-DRAINING LYMPH NODES AND MECHANISMS OF HOW VACCINATION PREVENTS LOCAL GENERATION OF MYELOID NICHES FOR MTB PERSISTENCE. SPECIFIC EFFORTS WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING THE MANUSCRIPT FOR PUBLICATION AND PERFORMING REVIEWER REQUESTED STUDIES.

II. CONTINUE EVALUATING THE DISTRIBUTION OF MTB ANTIGENS WITH RESPECT TO DISTINCT BACILLARY STATES WITHIN TISSUES. WE HAVE IDENTIFIED THAT MAJOR IMMUNODOMINANT ANTIGENS DO NOT APPEAR PHYSICALLY COUPLED WITH MTB BACILLI AND ARE OFTEN EXPORTED TO NEIGHBORING CELLS. THIS INDICATES THAT VACCINE EFFORTS AIMED AT ELICITING ADAPTIVE RESPONSES TO THOSE ANTIGENS WILL LARGELY FAIL TO AFFECT CELLS WHICH ARE ACTUALLY INFECTED WITH MTB – RATHER THE BYSTANDER CELLS CONTAINING ANTIGENS. UNDERSTANDING THESE PROCESSES WILL HELP IDENTIFY MECHANISMS OF VACCINE SUCCESS VS. FAILURE ALLOWING FOR CURBING MTB INFECTION AND ITS EVENTUAL PERSISTENCE.

III. IMPLEMENT ESTABLISHED HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES (LUNG AND LYMPH NODE) OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE. PREVIOUS EFFORTS IDENTIFIED DIVERSE GRANULOMA STRUCTURES IN LUNGS FROM DECEASED INDIVIDUALS WITH ADVANCED DISEASE. WE HAVE ALSO DEVELOPED EXTENSIVE ANTIBODY PANELS AGAINST MAJOR IMMUNE POPULATIONS OF INTEREST AS WELL AS IMPLEMENTED AN HIGHLY-MULTIPLEX ITERATIVE IMAGING TECHNIQUE, IBEX. UPCOMING WORK WILL USE THESE ADVANCED METHODS TO ELUCIDATE MAJOR STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF THESE LESIONS. WE WILL ALSO CONTINUE TO DISSECT HOW MTB INFECTION OCCURS WITHIN HUMAN LUNG-DRAINING LNS, DIRECTLY RELATING TO THE MURINE STUDY DESCRIBED ABOVE. 

IV. CONTINUE WITH ANALYSIS OF THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA FOR LUNG GRANULOMAS OVER THE EARLY COURSE OF INFECTION WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. WE HAVE COLLECTED LARGE NUMBERS OF SAMPLES OF EARLY LUNG LESIONS FOR THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS STUDY AND HAVE BEGUN ANALYSIS. MAJOR SLOWDOWNS IN WORK RESULTED DUE TO MICHAEL GALE’S LAB RELOCATING, BUT WE HAVE NOW BEGUN ANALYSIS WORK WITH JOHN AITCHINSON AND FERGUL DUFFY AT SCRI. IN THE COMING YEAR, THE GERNER LAB WILL FINALIZE ANALYSIS OF THE COLLECTED DATASET. 

V. ASSIST WITH MULTIOMICS ANALYSIS AND DATA INTERPRETATION FOR FLOW CYTOMETRY, SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA OBTAINED BY THE GERNER LAB AND OTHER GROUPS WITHIN THE IMPACTB CONSORTIUM. THIS WILL INVOLVE ANALYSIS OF CHEMOTACTIC AND ADHESION MOLECULES THAT MAY REGULATE CELLULAR POSITIONING, AS WELL AS HELPING IDENTIFY POTENTIA

THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT STATENS SERUM INSTITUT (SSI) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT.

THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, , SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB).

THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. 

OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB 

TASK 3.1: NHP SAFETY AND EFFICACY AGAINST ULTRA-LOW DOSE AEROSOL (ULDA) M.TB ERDMAN  
TO ENSURE THAT BIOLOGICAL RESULTS GENERATED IN THE VARIOUS CONSORTIUM LABS ARE COMPARABLE, WE WILL STANDARDIZE THE PRIMARY ASSAYS USED IN IMMUNOGENICITY ASSESSMENTS FOR EACH SPECIES. IN LINE WITH THE PROJECT GOALS TO DEVELOP A CROSS-SPECIES INTERROGATION PLATFORM, WE WILL HARMONIZE KEY ASSAYS ACROSS MULTIPLE SPECIES. SCRI WILL APPOINT AN OVERALL TASK LEADER TO COORDINATE AND OVERSEE THE WORK. ALL ASSAY STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES (SOP) WILL BE SHARED WITH A PRECLINICAL LABORATORY LEAD, DESIGNATED FOR EACH ASSAY, WHO WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HARMONIZING. FINAL SOPS WILL BE SHARED AND LEAD ASSAY LABS WILL CONDUCT SIDE-BY-SIDE TRAINING SESSIONS, AS WELL AS, MAINTAIN AND DISTRIBUTE COMMON REFERENCE STANDARDS AND REAGENTS, SUCH AS IDENTICAL STIMULATION ANTIGENS (BCG, PPD, SEB, PEPTIDE POOLS AS DESCRIBED BELOW (NTM MEGAPOOL, MTB300, MTB300-ID93, AND MTB300-M72),  15-MER PEPTIDES FOR ID93, COMPONENTS OF ID93, AND M72,AND UNSTIMULATED) AND BCG VACCINATION STRAIN (BCG AJ/BCG SSI). THESE REGENTS WILL BE INCLUDED IN AN OPTIMIZED MULTICOLOR IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE PANEL (OMIP). 
FURTHERMORE, SSI WILL ASSIST IN THE ANALYSIS OF REACTIVITY OF PEPTIDES IN HUMAN AND ANIMAL MODELS IN ANTIGENICITY ASSAYS PRIOR TO IMPLEMENTATION IN OPTIONS 1-4.
A POOL OF 15-MER T CELL EPITOPES WHICH ARE FOUND IN DIVERSE NTMS BUT ABSENT FROM M.TB (PMID: 25548174) WILL BE SUPPLIED BY  SSI IN THE OPTION 3 PERIOD TO COLLABORATOR LABS THAT REQUIRE THEM FOR IMMUNE PHENOTYPING ASSAYS. TAKING ADVANTAGE OF THE RECENTLY DEVELOPED APPROACH OF COMBINING A LARGE NUMBER OF EPITOPES IN ONE SINGLE POOL AS A "MEGAPOOL" (PMID: 27409590) WE COMBINE ALL EPITOPES IDENTIFIED IN THE PNAS STUDY TOGETHER WITH PEPTIDES IDENTIFIED BY OTHER MEMBERS OF OUR GROUP (PMID: 22046285). IN SUMMARY, LJI AND/OR SSI WILL PROVIDE: 
A.	MEGAPOOL OF 15-MER T CELL EPITOPES WHICH ARE FOUND IN DIVERSE NTMS BUT ABSENT FROM M.TB 
B.	MEGAPOOL OF M.TB -DERIVED EPITOPES (MTB300).
C.	MEGAPOOL OF M.TB -DERIVED EPITOPES FROM WHICH ID93-DERIVED EPITOPES WERE OMITTED (MTB300-ID93).
D.	MEGAPOOL OF M.TB-DERIVED EPITOPES FROM WHICH M72-DERIVED EPITOPES WERE OMITTED (MTB300-M72)

THE TARGET PATHOGENS ARE NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE AND CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS. STI SCOUT WILL ENABLE PCR-LEVEL ACCURACY WITH THE CONVENIENCE AND COST OF RAPID ANTIGEN TESTING. COSTS OF GOODS SOLD ARE PROJECTED TO BE FAR LOWER THAN COMPETITIVE PRODUCTS, MAKING IT FINANCIALLY VIABLE TO ENTER GLOBAL LOW RESOURCE MARKETS. THE SCOUT PLATFORM INCLUDES A SCOUT HUB—A LOW-COST REUSABLE DEVICE—AND THE SCOUT CONNECT MOBILE APPLICATION FOR IOS AND ANDROID OS. TOGETHER, THESE ENABLE TESTING FOR A DEVELOPING MENU OF INDICATIONS, NOT JUST STIS, AND PERMIT RESULT TRACKING, SECURE SHARING, AND FOLLOW-ON CARE VIA TELEHEALTH.
SCOUT WAS PREVIOUSLY AWARDED A CARB-X SEED AWARD CONTRACT TO DEMONSTRATE LOOP-DE-LOOP (LDL) CHEMISTRY WITH CRUDE PATIENT SAMPLES (URINE, VAGINAL SWABS). SCOUT SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED ALL MILESTONES WITHIN THE SEED CONTRACT AND DEMONSTRATED ANALYTICAL PERFORMANCE IN POSITIVE AND PATIENT SPIKED SAMPLES THAT EXCEEDED THE TARGETS SET WITHIN THE CONTRACT.
IN THIS DEVELOPMENT STAGE WORK, SCOUT WILL GENERATE ROBUST DATA AND DOCUMENTATION TO REACH DESIGN LOCK FOR STI SCOUT IN ADVANCE OF DOWNSTREAM FORMAL VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION ACTIVITIES THAT WILL EVENTUALLY SUPPORT A WHO PREQUALIFICATION AND US FDA 510(K) CLEARANCE. SCOUT WILL COMPLETE ASSAY DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES TO ENHANCE BOTH PERFORMANCE AND REGULATORY ALIGNMENT WITH WHO DRAFT TECHNICAL GUIDANCE. STI SCOUT PERFORMANCE AGAINST DESIGN INPUT REQUIREMENTS WILL BE ASSESSED ON THE INTEGRATED SCOUT SYSTEM (SCOUT HUB, SCOUT CONNECT APP) USING CONTROLLED TEST PROTOCOLS TO PROVIDE A SCIENTIFICALLY SOUND AND STATISTICALLY RIGOROUS EVALUATIONS. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PHASE WILL BE A CLEAR, DE-RISKED PATH TO INTERNATIONAL AND US COMMERCIALIZATION OF STI SCOUT, WITH SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AND EARLY PERFORMANCE AND USABILITY DATA TO INFORM FUTURE PIVOTAL STUDIES.
IN ALIGNMENT WITH CARB-X’S MISSION TO COMBAT THE GROWING THREAT OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE, SCOUT WILL ALSO ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY OF EXPANDING THE STI SCOUT PLATFORM TO DETECT NUCLEIC ACID MARKERS OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (AMR) ALONGSIDE PATHOGEN IDENTIFICATION.

THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-CRYOEM WILL ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) A PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS PROJECT AND WILL SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED.
A.
STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM:
UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE.
PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING.
B.
PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS:
UW-CRYOEM WILL LEAD A STUDY ENTITLED “MARBURG VIRUS GLYCOPROTEIN CHARACTERIZATION FOR ANTIGEN DESIGN.”
C.
QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING:

ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. 

GERNER LAB (YEAR 6 BASE) 

THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB), THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN.

IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MTB SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF VARIOUS CHEMOTACTIC OR ADHESION MOLECULES IN GUIDING IMMUNE CELLS TO VARIOUS SITES WITHIN THE INFECTED LUNG TISSUES AND LYMPHOID ORGANS, AS WELL AS IN MEDIATING PROTECTION FROM MTB INFECTION. IN YEAR 6, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL:

I. CONTINUE IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MTB INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. SUBSTANTIAL EFFORT WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING STUDIES DESCRIBING THE ROLE OF NEUTROPHILS IN SHAPING LUNG GRANULOMA STRUCTURE AND IN IMMUNOREGULATION WITHIN THE GRANULOMA.

II. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT EXPERIMENTS AIMED TO ELUCIDATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES WITHIN DRAINING LYMPH NODES DURING MTB INFECTION, WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. SPECIFIC EFFORTS WILL BE PLACED ON ELUCIDATION OF CHANGES OCCURRING WITHIN THE MYELOID COMPARTMENT IN LYMPH NODES WHICH PROMOTE VERSUS INHIBIT FUNCTIONAL T CELL ACTIVATION AT DIFFERENT TIMEPOINTS DURING INFECTION. ADDITIONAL WORK WILL INVESTIGATE HOW BCG VACCINATION INHIBITS THE GENERATION OF MYELOID MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LNS WHICH SERVE AS A NICHE FOR CHRONIC MTB PERSISTENCE.

III. CONTINUE DEVELOPMENT OF HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES (LUNG AND LYMPH NODE) OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE. PREVIOUS EFFORTS IDENTIFIED DIVERSE GRANULOMA STRUCTURES IN LUNGS FROM DECEASED INDIVIDUALS WITH ADVANCED DISEASE. UPCOMING WORK WILL ELUCIDATE ADDITIONAL IMMUNOLOGICAL FEATURES OF THESE STRUCTURES AND HOW THESE RELATE TO PROCESSES WITHIN THE DRAINING LNS. SPECIFIC GOAL WILL BE TO INVESTIGATE THE MICROANATOMY OF MTB INFECTION IN LUNG-DRAINING LNS, INCLUDING THE CELL TYPES, SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION, AND FUNCTIONAL STATES OF THE INFECTED CELLS. COMPARATIVE ANALYSES WITH MOUSE MODELS OF INFECTION (POINT II ABOVE) WILL BE PERFORMED.

Sub-Award Description:
IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A NEW TYPE OF ADJUVANTED VACCINE THAT BOTH ACTIVATES AND LIMITS THE
INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE. IN PRELIMINARY WORK, WE SHOWED THAT ADDING MOLECULES THAT ALTER THE SIGNALING OF
THE NF-􀈛􀀥 AND IRF PATHWAY IN COMBINATION WITH A WELL-CHARACTERIZED TLR AGONIST RESULTED IN NEAR-ZERO
SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION WHILE MAINTAINING MINIMAL LOCAL INFLAMMATION. AT THE SAME TIME, ADDITION OF THIS
COMPOUND, PME-564, INCREASED AND MODIFIED ANTIBODY RESPONSES FOR SEVERAL COMMERCIAL VACCINES – MOST
NOTABLY FLUZONE. IN THIS WORK, WE PROPOSE TO FURTHER DEVELOP THIS COMPOUND, PME-564, ALONGSIDE MRNA
VACCINES TO FIND A SINGLE ADJUVANT FORMULATION THAT CAN BE USED IN AN IMPROVED H5N1 VACCINE.
WE HAVE TWO GOALS:
(1) IDENTIFY A FORMULATION CANDIDATE THAT CAN BE RAPIDLY ADMIXED WITH EITHER CURRENT QUADRIVALENT FLU
VACCINES OR MRNA VACCINES. PAIRING THESE FORMULATIONS WITH THE HIGHEST PERFORMING VACCINE PLATFORM
TO DEVELOP VACCINE CANDIDATES. IMPROVING REACTOGENICITY, REDUCING DOSAGE, AND INCREASING DURABILITY OF
EACH VACCINE.
(2) RAPIDLY TESTING THESE CANDIDATES FOR COMPATIBILITY WITH COMMERCIAL VACCINE SYSTEMS AND PRE-CLINICAL
PANDEMIC FLU VACCINES, DETERMINING AN APPROPRIATE TOXICITY AND SAFETY PROFILE FOR BOTH THE INDEPENDENT
AND MIXED FORMULATION.
THIS NEW APPROACH ADDRESSES A LIMITATION IN CURRENT ADJUVANT TECHNOLOGY. ADJUVANTS TRANSITIONING OUT OF
BASIC DISCOVERY HAVE LIMITED METHODS TO CONTROL EXCESS INFLAMMATION IN THE FORM OF INCREASED CYTOKINES –
REPRESENTED BY EXCESS TNF-􀄮􀀃􀁄􀁑􀁇􀀃􀀬􀀯-6 PRODUCTION. THE FOCUS OF THIS SUPPLEMENTAL PROGRAM WILL BE THE COFORMULATION
OF THESE MOLECULES WITH MRNA VACCINES, SPECIFICALLY IN THE CONTEXT OF PANDEMIC FLU.
FORMULATIONS DO HELP ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM TO SOME EXTENT, BUT THEY DO NOT ADDRESS THE FUNDAMENTAL
ACTIVITY OF THE COMPOUND, WHICH GENERATES A LARGE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AT THE CELLULAR LEVEL. OUR
APPROACH DIRECTLY TARGETS THE PATHWAY THAT CAUSES THIS EXCESSIVE AND OFTEN SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AND
REDUCES IT. THE ADDED BENEFIT IS THAT BECAUSE THE MODULATION OCCURS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE AGONIST, IT CAN
PROVIDE AN ADDED BENEFIT NOT JUST TO A SPECIFIC AGONIST BUT TO ANY H5N1, QUADRIVALENT, OR MRNA FLU VACCINE.
THE RESULT IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE BUT EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, A BROAD INCREASE IN ANTIBODY RESPONSES FOR THESE
VACCINES.
AS WELL, EXPERIMENTS IN FORMULATION, DOSAGE, AND CONCENTRATION WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL INFORMATION FOR
DEFINING HOW IMMUNE-MODULATORS SUCH AS PME-564 ARE CONSIDERED IN USE IN VACCINE FORMULATIONS.
WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE THE USE OF OUR IMMUNOMODULATOR IN THE CONTEXT OF DOSE SPARING FOR PANDEMIC FLU
VACCINES. IF NEEDED, SEPARATE VIALS OF IMMUNOMODULATOR CAN BE CO-MIXED ON SITE OF VACCINATION WHICH WILL
ENABLE DOSE SPARING FOR AVAILABLE VACCINES. WE WILL EXPLORE MAXIMAL AND MINIMAL DOSES OF MRNA IN
COMBINATION WITH OUR IMMUNOMODULATORS TO SELECT THE BEST BALANCE BETWEEN DURABILITY, IMMUNOGENICITY,
AND REACTOGENICITY.
OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP AN ADJUVANT FORMULATION THAT INCREASES THE NEUTRALIZING IGG LEVELS
AND DURABILITY OF THOSE LEVELS FOR A PLATFORM OF MRNA VACCINES WITH A FOCUS ON H5N1 FLU SYSTEMS WHILE
MINIMIZING THE INFLAMMATORY EFFECTS UPON INJECTION.
OUR SECONDARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF IMMUNOMODULATORY COMPOUND PME-564
􀀋􀀥􀁄􀁉􀁈􀁗􀁌􀁑􀁌􀁅􀀌􀀃􀁄􀁖􀀃􀁄􀀃􀁅􀁕􀁒􀁄􀁇-SPECTRUM VACCINE ENHANCING OR DOSE SPARING EXCIPIENT THAT CAN BE USED AS PART OF
MULTIPLE FORMULATIONS.
TO IMPROVE THE OUTCOME OF THE FORMULATION AND TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF PME-􀀘􀀙􀀗􀀃􀀋􀀥􀁄􀁉􀁈􀁗􀁌􀁑􀁌􀁅􀀌􀀏􀀃􀁚􀁈􀀃
WILL EXPLORE THE MECHANISM OF A SERIES OF CHEMICALLY SYNTHESIZED DERIVATIVES, OPTIMIZE THEIR STRUCTURE AND
FORMULATION, AND TEST THEM AS ADJUVANTS WITH MULTIPLE FLU VACCINATION PLATFORMS. THESE VACCINE CANDIDATES
WILL THEN BE TESTED FOR SAFETY, TOXICITY, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE PROTECTION IN MOUSE CHALLENGE BEFORE BEING
USED IN HIGHER ANIMAL MODELS.

THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UK HEALTH SECURITY AGENCY (UKHSA), PREVIOUSLY KNOWN AS PUBLIC HEALTH ENGLAND (PHE), WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT.

THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB).

THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP-DERIVED SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. 

OPTION 2 ACTIVITIES: OBJECTIVE: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN GUINEA PIG MODEL OF TB

TASK 2.1 EVALUATE IMMUNE RESPONSE OF TB CANDIDATE VACCINES IN GUINEA PIGS

GUINEA PIG IMMUNOLOGY
THE ABILITY TO STUDY IMMUNE RESPONSES IN GUINEA PIGS IS SLOWLY IMPROVING. METHODOLOGY FOR DETERMINING A VARIETY OF CELL- SURFACE MARKERS, CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES HAS BEEN DEVELOPED AND STUDIES HAVE BEEN PERFORMED ON BCG-VACCINATED AND M.TB-INFECTED GUINEA PIGS. RELATED SOPS DEVELOPED AT PARTNER INSTITUTES LIKE CSU WILL BE SHARED WITH UKHSA FOR PERFORMANCE OF GUINEA PIG ENDPOINTS AND ASSAY HARMONIZATION. THE NUMBER OF ANTIBODY REAGENTS REMAINS RESTRICTIVE BUT SOME KEY FEATURES OF THE IMMUNE RESPONSE HAVE BEEN DESCRIBED. USING FLOW CYTOMETRY, IT IS POSSIBLE TO MONITOR CD4 AND CD8 T CELLS IN THE LUNGS AND STAINING WITH CD62L PLUS GATING VERSUS CD45 CAN IDENTIFY ACTIVATED T CELLS. FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIBODIES TO DETECT IFN-Γ WILL ENABLE INTRACELLULAR STAINING PROTOCOLS TO BE ESTABLISHED. FLOW CYTOMETRY STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT CELL ACCUMULATION PATTERNS CHANGE IN BCG VACCINATED GUINEA PIGS AFTER AEROSOL CHALLENGE AND THAT THESE PATTERNS DIFFER FROM THOSE OF THE UNVACCINATED CONTROLS; FOR EXAMPLE, ACTIVATED CD4+ RESPONSES HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO APPEAR MORE RAPIDLY AND THERE WAS A FASTER AND LARGER MACROPHAGE RESPONSE POST-INFECTION IN BCG VACCINATED ANIMALS THAN IN UNVACCINATED CONTROLS. SUCH FINDINGS OFFER THE POTENTIAL FOR IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION BOTH PRE- AND POST- CHALLENGE. THERE IS NOW A LARGE PANEL OF CYTOKINES (IL-1, IL-4, IL-10, IL-12P40, IFN-Γ, AND TNFΑ) AND CHEMOKINES (IL- 8, MCP-1, TGFΒ, AND RANTES) THAT CAN BE MEASURED BY PCR. THERE ARE A SMALL NUMBER OF ANTIBODY REAGENTS SPECIFIC FOR SOME OF THESE CYTOKINES BEING DEVELOPED BY OUR GROUP AND OTHERS WHICH WILL INCREASE THE SOPHISTICATION OF THESE STUDIES. WORK BY OTHER GROUPS USED MOUSE ANTIBODIES IN A MULTIPLEX ASSAY TO DETECT GUINEA PIG CYTOKINES AND WE PROPOSE TO EVALUATE THIS SYSTEM ON SERA AND ANTIGEN-STIMULATED CELL SUPERNATANTS.

CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES: WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED AN IFN-Γ ELISPOT. INITIATIVES TO FURTHER OPTIMIZE THIS ASSAY ARE ON- GOING. IF SUCH ASSAYS BECOME AVAILABLE, THEY WILL BE USED TO DETECT IFNΓ SECRETION BY CELLS IN WHOLE BLOOD, PMBC OR SPLENOCYTES STIMULATED WITH APPROPRIATE ANTIGENS. Sub-Award Description:
THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON NMR GROUP (UW-NMR), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GABRIELE VARANI,
PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-NMR WILL
BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING 1 NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS ONE YEAR SUBCONTRACT PERIOD, 9/1/2025 –
8/31/2026) AND FOR LEADING ONE PROJECT ON PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO
OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS.
A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULE BY NMR:
UW-NMR WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES USING
NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID
CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES AND
ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-NMR WORK.
THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25 KDA THAT FAIL TO
PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED FROM
COMMUNITY REQUESTS AND INTERNAL BATCHES; SPECIFICALLY, THESE WILL BE TARGETS OF INTEREST TO THE
CENTER THAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED USING CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. HOWEVER, DR. VARANI WILL ALSO
IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE
AND ARE WILLING TO COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID, ESPECIALLY IN THE
AREA OF BACTERIAL AND VIRAL NON CODING RNAS. UW-NMR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT
HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP)
AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC
LEADERSHIP TEAM, WHENEVER OPPORTUNITIES ARISE FOR ADVANCING SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS THAT MIGHT
BEST BE ADDRESSED BY NMR.
CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA
COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE
EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE
PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE
RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED
ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF
STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY,
THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA
BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL
1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK
(BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE
STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE.
B. LEAD ONE PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS
PROJECT.
THE UN-NMR GROUP WILL LEAD A PROJECT ENTITLED “STRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATION OF AN ESSENTIAL
RNA PACKAGING ELEMENT FROM THE INFLUENZA A VIRUS.”
C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING:
UW-NMR WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE
THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA ON WELL-DEFINED PROTEIN AND RNA SAMPLES. UW-NMR WILL
ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH
THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING
SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND
NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL CONTRIBUTE TO
QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED
AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL
PUBLICATIONS.
UW-NMR IS EXPECTED TO SOLVE AT LEAST 1 NMR STRUCTURE FROM THESE STUDIES DURING THIS
CONTRACT YEAR.

Sub-Award Description: DIAGNOSIS OF LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (LRTLS) OFTEN RELIES ON SAMPLE TYPES SUCH AS BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE OR ENDOTRACHEAL ASPIRATE, WHICH ARE HIGHLY INVASIVE, OR SPUTUM, WHICH IS MORE DIFFICULT TO OBTAIN IN CERTAIN PATIENTS. THESE SAMPLES ARE ESPECIALLY CHALLENGING TO COLLECT IN CHILDREN; WHERE RAPID DIAGNOSIS OF LRTLS IS CRUCIAL SINCE PNEUMONIA ACCOUNTS FOR 14% OF ALL DEATHS OF CHILDREN UNDER 5 YEARS OLD. BLOOD AS AN ALTERNATIVE SAMPLE TYPE WOULD BE MORE EASILY ACCESSIBLE IN ALL PATIENT GROUPS, INCLUDING NEWBORNS AND CHILDREN. DIAGNOSIS OF LRTLS IN CHILDREN REMAINS AN UNRESOLVED CHALLENGE AS THE DISEASE AETIOLOGY IS NOT ACHIEVED FOR THE MAJORITY OF CHILDREN, EVEN IN HIGH-INCOME COUNTRIES. CULTURE-BASED DIAGNOSTIC METHODS ARE SLOW AND HAVE POOR SENSITIVITY, WHILE MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTIC RESULTS LACK SPECIFICITY. WE DEMONSTRATED THAT BROAD APPLICATION OF MOLECULAR PATHOGEN DETECTION IN 4,611 FEBRILE PATIENTS IN THE EU-FUNDED PERFORM STUDY DID NOT ENABLE CONCLUSIVE DISCRIMINATION OF BACTERIAL OR VIRAL AETIOLOGY. VIRUSES ARE DETECTED IN MOST PATIENTS WITH BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, AND THE CLINICAL VALUE OF INDIVIDUAL PATHOGEN DETECTION IN DETERMINING TREATMENT IS LOW. NEW APPROACHES ARE NEEDED TO ACCURATELY AND RAPIDLY INFORM CLINICAL DECISIONS AND GUIDE ANTIBIOTIC THERAPY. WE ARE A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM OF MEDICAL DEVICE DEVELOPMENT ENGINEERS (PROTONDX), CLINICAL ACADEMIC DOCTORS WITH EXPERTISE IN PAEDIATRIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE, MOLECULAR BIOLOGISTS AND BIOINFORMATICIANS (IMPERIAL). OUR APPROACH - INSTEAD OF RELYING ON PATHOGEN DETECTION FROM LOWER RESPIRATORY SPECIMENS - RELIES ON QUANTIFICATION OF HOST BLOOD RNA BIOMARKERS, TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN BACTERIAL AND VIRAL DISEASES WITH HIGH ACCURACY. HOST RESPONSE CAN ALSO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN ACTIVE BACTERIAL INFECTION AND COLONIZATION, AS COLONIZATION OR LATENT INFECTION DOES NOT GIVE RISE TO THE SAME INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES OBSERVED IN DISEASE. ADDITIONALLY, VIA RNA-SEQ STUDIES WE HAVE EXAMINED AND PUBLISHED PROOF OF PRINCIPLE THAT THE LEVELS OF EXPRESSION OF MULTIPLE RNA BIOMARKERS MEASURED SIMULTANEOUSLY CAN ACHIEVE MULTICLASS CLASSIFICATION AT THE PATHOGEN LEVEL WITH HIGH SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO IDENTIFY SIGNATURES THAT CAN BE ASSESSED IN BLOOD VIA A LOOP MEDIATED ISOTHERMAL AMPLIFICATION (LAMP)-BASED HOST RESPONSE TEST TO DETECT INFECTIONS AND CLASSIFY THE MAJOR ORGANISMS CAUSING COMMUNITY ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP). THE WORK WILL DELIVER PROOF-OF-CONCEPT FOR BLOOD-BASED TESTING USING STANDARD QPCR PLATFORMS AND A TRANSFORMATIVE PORTABLE, ACCURATE, RAPID AND EASY-TO-USE SAMPLE-TO-RESULT DIAGNOSTIC TECHNOLOGY CALLED LACEWING. THE TEST WOULD PROVIDE A MULTI-OUTCOME PROBABILITY OF A PATIENT BELONGING TO EACH DIAGNOSTIC GROUP: BROAD LEVEL CLASSIFICATION (BACTERIAL, VIRAL, TB, OTHER CAUSES), AND DETAILED LEVEL CLASSIFICATION (IDENTIFICATION OF THE CAUSATIVE PATHOGEN). THE TESTING OUTPUTS WOULD ULTIMATELY INFORM CLINICAL DECISIONS IN EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS (EDS) AND URGENT CARE CENTRES IN <20 MINS WITHOUT A LABORATORY AND SKILLED PERSONNEL. WE WILL FOCUS ON CHILDREN UNDER 2 YEARS OLD, WHICH ARE A HIGH-RISK POPULATION FOR CAP WHERE INVASIVE SAMPLE TYPES ARE EVEN LESS ACCESSIBLE. WE WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING RNA BIOMARKER DATA USING A NOVEL CROSS-PLATFORM BIOINFORMATIC FRAMEWORK FOR SIGNATURE DISCOVERY AND TRANSLATION THAT WILL BE COMPATIBLE WITH LAB-BASED OR POINT OF CARE DIAGNOSTIC TECHNOLOGIES AND PLATFORMS. OUR FRAMEWORK INCORPORATES PLATFORM-SPECIFIC CONSTRAINTS EARLY IN THE BIOMARKER DISCOVERY AND SELECTION PHASES TO ADDRESS PRECISION-RELATED CHALLENGES AND MAXIMISE TEST DEVELOPMENT FEASIBILITY. TESTING WILL BE CONDUCTED ON A REAL-TIME LAMP (QLAMP) PLATFORM WITH PRELIMINARY COMPARISON TO OUR LAB-ON-CHIP ELECTROCHEMICAL SENSING LACEWING PLATFORM IN SEMICONDUCTOR TECHNOLOGY FOR REAL-TIME ELECTRONIC LAMP (ELAMP), WHICH HAS ALREADY BEEN DEMONSTRATED WITH BLOOD AND OTHER SAMPLE TYPES FOR TARGETS INCLUDING SARS-COV-2, DENGUE, COLISTIN RESISTANCE AND KLEBSIELLA.

Sub-Award Description: THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM WILL EVALUATE THE POTENTIAL OF BREATH ANALYSIS AS A NOVEL, NONINVASIVE DIAGNOSTIC APPROACH FOR LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (LRTIS). THE GOAL IS TO ASSESS WHETHER MEASURING VOLATILE ORGANIC COMPOUNDS (VOCS) IN EXHALED BREATH CAN PROVIDE RAPID, ACCURATE, AND CLINICALLY USEFUL DIAGNOSTIC INFORMATION TO SUPPORT PATIENT CARE. THE PROJECT IS STRUCTURED AROUND A PROSPECTIVE, MULTI-SITE CLINICAL STUDY INVOLVING MULTIPLE PATIENT POPULATIONS INCLUDING BOTH CHILDREN AND ADULTS, IN CONVENTIONAL AND INTENSIVE CARE SETTINGS. BREATH SAMPLES AND MICROBIOLOGICAL SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED ALONGSIDE STANDARD CLINICAL AND BIOLOGICAL DATA TO DOCUMENT THE DIAGNOSTIC SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS USING REAL-TIME MASS SPECTROMETRY. THE PROGRAM WILL ASSESS WHETHER BREATH-BASED DIAGNOSTICS CAN DIFFERENTIATE INFECTION FROM COLONIZATION, HELP IDENTIFY THE PATHOGENS, AND REACH RELEVANT DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY COMPARED TO CURRENT REFERENCE METHODS. Sub-Award Description:
THE WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY GROUP (WSU), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GARRY BUCHKO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENTS. WSU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST ONE NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS YEAR OF THE CONTRACT (SEPT 1, 2025 THROUGH AUG 31, 2026) WHICH MAY BE FROM THE SSGCID PIPELINE OR MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH A SPECIAL PROJECT. WSU WILL LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-BASED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT PROJECT AND MAY SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR).
A.
STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY NMR:
WSU (DR. BUCHKO) WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST ONE PROTEIN USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE, AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE WSU/PNNL-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE SEATTLE CHILDREN’S RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP, HOWEVER, DR. BUCHKO WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID. WSU MAY BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM.
CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY WSU. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND SIDE CHAIN 1H, 13C, AND 15N RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C, AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE.
B.
LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-BASED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT (SVTD)
WSU WILL LEAD A SVTD PROJECT ENTITLED “CHARACTERIZATION OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS TARGETING HELICOBACTER PYLORI.”
C.
QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION, AND REPORTING:
WSU WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. WSU WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS, AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUESTED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. THE MAJOR AIM OF THE PROJECT WORK WILL BE IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

Sub-Award Description: SERES IS DEVELOPING A NOVEL LIVE BIOTHERAPEUTIC PRODUCT (LBP) OF HUMAN COMMENSAL BACTERIA FORMULATED FOR ORAL LIQUID DELIVERY, TO ADDRESS THE UNMET NEED FOR PREVENTION OF GUT-SEEDED AMR INFECTION IN THE MEDICAL ICU. INFECTIONS WITH PATHOGENIC (OFTEN MULTIDRUG RESISTANT, MDR) BACTERIA ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF MORTALITY IN THE MEDICAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU), CAUSING UP TO 9 DEATHS FOR EVERY 100 ICU PATIENTS ADMITTED (VINCENT, 2009). MOST PATIENTS ARE ADMITTED TO THE MEDICAL ICU WITH A KNOWN OR SUSPECTED INFECTION (I.E., SEPSIS) BUT, WITH TARGETED OR EMPIRIC ANTIBIOTICS, MOST RECOVER FROM THIS INITIAL INFECTION. WHAT CAUSES DEATHS—AND WHAT THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO PREVENT—ARE THE SECONDARY, HEALTHCARE- ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS THAT FREQUENTLY DEVELOP DURING THE PROLONGED RECOVERY FROM SEPSIS. A NOVEL APPROACH THAT ADDRESSES BOTH GUT COLONIZATION AND SUBSEQUENT TRANSLOCATION BY E. COLI AND OTHER GUT SEEDED PATHOGENS COULD PREVENT A SIGNIFICANT PROPORTION OF THESE INFECTIONS. IF GUT COLONIZATION AND TRANSLOCATION BY E. COLI COULD BE AMELIORATED BY A LBP SUCH AS SER-155, A LARGE PROPORTION OF THESE INFECTIONS COULD BE PREVENTED. SER-155 IS CURRENTLY IN CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT AND HAS BEEN EVALUATED IN ALLOGENEIC HCT PATIENTS. DATA FROM OUR PHASE 1B STUDY SUPPORTS THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF SER-155 IN PREVENTING INFECTION IN IMMUNE COMPROMISED, HOSPITALIZED PATIENTS. THE PROPOSED WORK WILL EXTEND THESE FINDINGS BY DEVELOPING A LIQUID FORMULATION OF SER-155 (“SER-155-LF"), A NECESSARY STEP IN THE MEDICAL ICU AS PATIENTS ARE COMMONLY INTUBATED WITH NARROW-CALIBER GASTRIC OR DUODENAL FEEDING TUBES, PLACED FOR THE DELIVERY OF MEDICATIONS AND ENTERAL NUTRITION. UPON SUCCESSFUL DEVELOPMENT OF A LIQUID FORMULATION WHICH IS SUITED FOR DELIVERY IN THE ICU VIA NG TUBE, THE PROPOSED WORK PLAN WILL NEXT FOCUS ON GMP MANUFACTURING OF SER-155-LF FOR CLINICAL STUDY AND PREPARATION OF AN EARLY PHASE TRIAL IN ICU PATIENTS WITH A PRIMARY OUTCOME OF SAFETY AND ENGRAFTMENT, EXPLORATORY ENDPOINTS AROUND E. COLI COLONIZATION AND AMR, AND DENSE DOWNSTREAM CLINICAL AND MECHANISTIC ANALYSES.

THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT FRED HUTCHINSON CANCER CENTER (FHCC) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT.

ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. 

THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA VACCINE DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB)

THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. 

OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB

TASK 3.5 TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS OF NHP SAMPLES. 
FHCC WILL EXECUTE GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING WITH RNASEQ/NANOSTRING ASSAYS ON NHP SAMPLES GENERATED IN OPTION 3 AT UKHSA. TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS WILL BE FOCUSED ON IDENTIFYING A PERIPHERAL BLOOD SURROGATE ENDPOINT FOR THE M.TB ERDMAN ULDA CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. THE INITIAL UNBIASED RNA SEQUENCING APPROACH WILL USE WHOLE-BLOOD SAMPLES FROM PRE- AND POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL LOOK FOR TRANSCRIPTS THAT ARE CORRELATED WITH M.TB COLONY FORMING UNITS (CFU) AND M.TB QPCR ASSAYS FROM BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL), THE PRIMARY CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. IN ADDITION TO ABSOLUTE ABUNDANCE AT POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS, WE WILL ALSO LOOK FOR CHANGES IN TRANSCRIPT ABUNDANCE RELATIVE TO THE DAY OF CHALLENGE AS A POTENTIAL CORRELATE OF CHALLENGE OUTCOME. AS WE BUILD A MODEL TO PREDICT CHALLENGE OUTCOME FROM THESE GENE EXPRESSION MEASURES WE WILL SPECIFICALLY CONSIDER TRANSCRIPTS THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN IDENTIFIED AS PREDICTORS OF PROGRESSION TO TB DISEASE, SUCH AS TYPE I IFN-RELATED GENES WHOSE EXPRESSION INCREASES DURING DISEASE PROGRESSION. THE HUMAN EXPRESSION SIGNATURES WILL BE EVALUATED IN NHPS AND VICE VERSA; ADDITIONALLY, A JOINT MODEL WILL BE DEVELOPED, ALLOWING FOR DIFFERENCES IN NHP AND HUMAN ASSOCIATIONS, WHILE IDENTIFYING A COMMON GENE SIGNATURE. ONCE TRANSCRIPTS OR GENES HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED, A TARGETED CROSS-SPECIES NANOSTRING PANEL WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR EVALUATION IN THE SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AS WELL AS IN FUTURE NHP AND CLINICAL TRIALS. WE PLAN TO DEVELOP A NANOSTRING NCOUNTER GENE PANEL WHICH CAN ACCOMMODATE UP TO 800 GENES AND WOULD BE SIGNIFICANTLY MORE COST EFFECTIVE THAN RNA SEQUENCING. ALTERNATIVELY, DEPENDING ON THE COMPLEXITY OF THE GENE PANEL, IT COULD BE DEVELOPED AS A 96 TRANSCRIPT/GENE (INCLUDING HOUSEKEEPING GENES) QPCR BIOMARK FLUIDIGM ASSAY.

EXPERIMENTAL DATA WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE STATISTICAL CENTER AND A FORMAL INTER-SITE AND INTER-SPECIES VARIABILITY ASSESSMENT WILL BE PERFORMED. VARIABILITY WILL BE DETERMINED USING COEFFICIENTS OF VARIATION (CV), MEAN AND STANDARD DEVIATION OF RESPONSES. DESIRED CUT-OFFS FOR ACCEPTABLE CVS WILL BE PRE-SPECIFIED FOR EACH ASSAY. EFFORT IN THE BASE PERIOD WILL HAVE BEEN MADE TO STANDARDIZE THE ASSAYS AND HARMONIZATION ASSESSMENTS WILL HAVE BEEN REPEATED IF CVS DID NOT MEET THE CUT OFF.
